items.question: What attainment makes a practitioner dear to the yoginis?
premises: Enjoyment and liberation together constitute a great accomplishment.
Such great accomplishment belongs to the practitioner.
This accomplishment makes one dear to the yoginis.
items.inference: A practitioner possessing the great accomplishment of enjoyment and liberation becomes dear to the yoginis.
items.plain_english: One who attains the great accomplishment of both enjoyment and liberation becomes dear to the yoginis.

items.question: Which chapter emerges in the context of Candra-dvipa?
premises: A chapter is identified as ninth in sequence.
This chapter is described as emerged in Candra-dvipa.
The location marks the chapter's context.
items.inference: The ninth chapter is the one that has emerged in Candra-dvipa.
items.plain_english: This is the ninth chapter, which emerged in Candra-dvipa.

items.question: In what posture should the practitioner visualize the self surrounded by fire?
premises: The self is visualized as surrounded by fire.
The self is described as standing.
The stance is supported on one foot.
items.inference: The practitioner should visualize the self surrounded by fire while standing on one foot.
items.plain_english: One should visualize oneself surrounded by fire, standing on one foot.

items.question: What has been revealed to the speaker by the divine teacher today?
premises: The speaker addresses the god directly.
The determination of knowledge is the subject revealed.
This revelation has been made manifest today to the speaker.
items.inference: The determination of knowledge has been made manifest to the speaker today by the god.
items.plain_english: O God, today the determination of knowledge has been made manifest to me.

items.question: What division does the speaker seek to understand completely and without limit?
premises: The object of inquiry is a division.
This division consists of eight octads.
The speaker seeks to know it fully and endlessly.
items.inference: The speaker seeks to know fully and endlessly the division of the eight octads.
items.plain_english: And I seek to know fully and endlessly the division of the eight octads.

items.question: How is accomplishment quickly attained in the secret place and wheel?
premises: The secret place and the wheel are the loci of practice.
Accomplishment occurs in relation to them.
The speaker asks Bhairava how this happens quickly.
items.inference: The question concerns the means by which the secret place and wheel are quickly accomplished.
uncertainties: The syntactic role of sthānaṃ and cakraṃ as joint subjects or topics is slightly ambiguous.
items.plain_english: O Bhairava, how is the secret place and the wheel quickly accomplished?

items.question: Why does Bhairava praise the goddess for asking about a matter rare even for gods?
premises: Bhairava expresses strong approval to the great goddess.
He states that he has been asked.
The matter asked about is hard for gods to obtain.
items.inference: Bhairava praises the goddess because her question concerns knowledge rare even among the gods.
items.plain_english: Well said, well said, O great goddess! I have been asked about something that is hard for even the gods to obtain.

items.question: Where are the syllables kṣa and laṃ located within the subtle body?
premises: The syllable kṣa is associated with the state of the brahmarandhra.
The syllable laṃ is associated with the forehead.
These assignments map syllables to bodily loci.
items.inference: The syllable kṣa is located at the brahmarandhra and the syllable laṃ at the forehead.
uncertainties: lalāṭayoḥ is dual in form though often used for the forehead region.
items.plain_english: The syllable kṣa is in the brahmarandhra, and the syllable laṃ is in the forehead.

items.question: Where are the syllables ṣa and śa situated in the body?
premises: The syllable ṣa is placed in the throat region.
The syllable śa is placed in the heart.
These placements continue the mapping of syllables to loci.
items.inference: The syllable ṣa is situated in the throat region and the syllable śa in the heart.
items.plain_english: The syllable ṣa is in the throat region, and the syllable śa is then in the heart.

items.question: What instruction follows the declaration of the place-wheels to the beloved?
premises: The place-wheels have been declared.
These wheels have an associated meditation.
The beloved is instructed to hear that meditation.
items.inference: After declaring the place-wheels, the teacher instructs the beloved to hear their meditation.
items.plain_english: Thus the place-wheels have been declared; now hear their meditation, O beloved.

items.question: How is the divine lotus of the first octad described in meditation?
premises: The lotus is described as divine.
It has eight spokes or petals.
It is adorned by the first octad.
items.inference: The meditation presents a divine eight-spoked lotus adorned by the first octad.
uncertainties: āra can mean spoke or petal in cakra imagery.
items.plain_english: One should contemplate a divine eight-spoked lotus adorned by the first octad.

rows.grounds: object to be abandoned; sandhi form

items.question: What conduct must a practitioner with equanimous mind abandon through practice?
premises: Practice leads to an equanimous mind.
Village duty represents conventional social conduct.
The practitioner is instructed to abandon that duty.
items.inference: Through practice, one whose mind becomes equanimous should abandon village duty.
items.plain_english: Through practice, with an equanimous mind, one should abandon the duties of village life.

items.question: What yogic powers arise from the practice described to the beloved?
premises: Knowledge of hearing from afar is named as a result.
Paralysis of bonds is named as another result.
These powers are presented together to the beloved.
items.inference: The practice yields the power of distant hearing and the paralysis of bonds.
uncertainties: stobha can imply arrest, stupefaction, or paralysis depending on context.
items.plain_english: O beloved, one gains the knowledge of hearing from afar and likewise the power to paralyze bonds.

items.question: What further attainments are briefly promised to the goddess?
premises: Immortality is named as an attainment.
Transformation is named as another attainment.
These are stated briefly to the goddess.
items.inference: The further attainments briefly promised are immortality and transformation.
items.plain_english: Likewise, O goddess, in brief, one attains immortality and transformation.

items.question: How is the second eight-petaled lotus characterized in this meditation?
premises: A second lotus is introduced.
It is described as eight-petaled.
It is well illuminated by meditation on fire.
items.inference: The second eight-petaled lotus is characterized as well illuminated by fiery meditation.
items.plain_english: The second is an eight-petaled lotus, well illuminated by meditation on fire.

items.question: What ability arises for one whose mind is absorbed in single-pointed meditation?
premises: The mind becomes absorbed in one-pointed meditation.
The practitioner performs an act of making form.
This form can be produced in many ways.
items.inference: One whose mind is absorbed in single-pointed meditation can assume many forms.
items.plain_english: One whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation can assume many forms.

items.question: What destructive power can an angered adept exercise over the triple world?
premises: The adept is described as angry.
The object of action is the entire triple world.
The triple world includes both moving and unmoving beings.
items.inference: When angry, the adept can destroy the entire triple world with all its moving and unmoving beings.
items.plain_english: When angry, he can destroy the entire triple world, with all that moves and does not move.

items.question: What liberating function is attributed to the third great wheel?
premises: A third great wheel is introduced.
It is described as a liberator.
Its liberating scope concerns the nine principles.
items.inference: The third great wheel functions as the liberator from the nine principles.
items.plain_english: The third great wheel is the liberator from the nine principles.

items.question: What bodily and perceptual powers result from this wheel's practice?
premises: Destruction of wrinkles and grey hair is named as a result.
Seeing from very far away is named as another result.
These results are presented together.
items.inference: The practice yields the removal of wrinkles and grey hair and the power of seeing from very far away.
items.plain_english: One gains the destruction of wrinkles and grey hair, and likewise the ability to see from very far away.

items.question: How should a practitioner devoted to meditation act in solitude?
premises: The practitioner is situated in solitude.
The practitioner is intent on meditation.
The instruction is to make many forms.
items.inference: A practitioner intent on meditation should, in solitude, create many forms.
items.plain_english: In solitude, intent on meditation, create many forms.

items.question: What attainment comes to one devoted to constant practice?
premises: The practitioner is devoted to constant practice.
The verb indicates the production or attainment of a state.
The state attained is immortality.
items.inference: One devoted to constant practice indeed attains immortality.
items.plain_english: Indeed, one who is devoted to constant practice attains immortality.

items.question: What fate follows from abstaining from food for a day in this practice?
premises: The condition described is non-eating for a day.
The result concerns death related to age.
The verb indicates a future going to that death.
items.inference: By abstaining from food for a day, one will go to death by aging.
uncertainties: The exact sense of vayo mṛtyuṃ as death by age or the death of age is contextually compressed.
items.plain_english: By not eating for a day, one will go to death by aging.

items.question: What bodily form results from constant yogic practice over sixteen years?
premises: The means is yoga with constant practice.
The duration indicated is two times eight years.
The result is becoming a form of that age.
items.inference: Through constant yogic practice, one may attain the form of a sixteen-year-old.
items.plain_english: Through constant yogic practice, one attains the form of a sixteen-year-old.

items.question: What effect follows from always contemplating the triple world as smoke-colored?
premises: The triple world is to be contemplated as smoke-colored.
This contemplation is to be done always.
The result is the ability to shake the triple world.
items.inference: By always contemplating the triple world as smoke-colored, one may shake the triple world.
items.plain_english: O beloved, by always contemplating the triple world as smoke-colored, one can shake the triple world.
